title: Forking conversations in Grove
summary: Create independent conversations from a completed source turn, preserving provider context and explicit lineage.

sources.text: Look into how t3code does it and let's plan the ability to fork conversations

scope: No workspace rollback or merge-back in the initial scope

claims.text: A user can fork a completed conversation into a new session.
claims.detail: Offer Fork from the session menu and from a completed response; show the source and open the new session. Disable with an explanation when a stable source is unavailable. Keep the parent running and its draft intact.

options.label: Any completed response
options.description: Allow branching from a stable earlier turn and from the latest response.

options.label: Latest response only
options.description: Reduce the first release to the current completed conversation.

claims.text: The new session continues with the selected provider context.
claims.detail: Persist a pending source recipe before launch; resolve it through the provider adapter. Never resume the parent as the child or silently present copied text as native context. Surface failures and allow retry without damaging the parent. Validate exact turn-boundary behavior against installed provider versions before promising it.

entries.title: Record source and new session identity
entries.detail: Save parent key, provider session reference, selected stable turn and pending state.

entries.title: Resolve provider fork
entries.detail: Codex: investigate thread/fork and earlier-turn boundary support. Claude: adapt the existing --fork-session and --resume-session-at recipe; confirm response anchor semantics.

entries.title: Commit child provider identity
entries.detail: Persist the new provider session ID and reconcile history; retain the recipe across restart until durable.

decisions.prompt: What happens when native context cannot be forked?

options.label: Explain and stop
options.description: Preserve context fidelity and offer retry; no silent fallback.

options.label: Offer text handoff
options.description: Explicitly offer a new session with limited transcript context; disclose omissions.

children.text: Existing session records provide a starting point.
children.detail: SavedSession stores provider, key, thread_id, transcript and ClaudeResume; Claude uses a durable fork recipe for edits. Codex currently starts or resumes a thread. Extend these paths without reusing edit rollback.

exhibit.text: SavedSession { key, provider, thread_id, items, claude_resume, pending_edit, … }

claims.text: Forks make their workspace relationship clear.
claims.detail: Default to the same checkout and current filesystem state. A conversation fork does not restore files to their state at the source turn; both sessions can modify the same files. Make that visible at creation.

nodes.text: Uses the current checkout and its current files. Both conversations share changes.

decisions.prompt: Where should the new conversation work?

options.label: Same checkout
options.description: Fast, with shared live files and no Git operation.

options.label: Offer checkout choice
options.description: Include an existing or new worktree flow; requires additional design and handling of uncommitted changes.

claims.text: Users can find the source and revisit the fork.
claims.detail: Persist parent session key and source turn metadata independently of provider IDs. Show a navigable source link and a fork indicator in existing session navigation. A missing or deleted parent leaves the child usable. Copy only historical transcript through the boundary; exclude drafts, queued actions, active approvals and transient state.

exhibit.text: ForkLineage { parent_key: String, source_turn: StableTurnRef, provider_source: ProviderRef, resolution: Pending | Resolved | Failed }

claims.text: Forks survive restart and keep both conversations independent.
claims.detail: Test source boundary, parent preservation, child identity, duplicate activation, restart before and after first send, missing source and provider errors. Run live Codex and live Claude checks separately, recording version and results; fixtures are not provider verification. Inspect native navigation, focus, disabled and error states, narrow widths and themes using the Grove UI contract. Run relevant checks and ./install.sh once after final code changes unless delivery instructions change.

entries.title: Provider checks
entries.detail: For Codex and Claude, verify context before and after the selected response and prove parent and child diverge independently; report untested or unsupported boundaries.

entries.title: Native UI checks
entries.detail: Inspect actual controls, navigation, keyboard focus and error states; record platform coverage.
